name: Example: Proving the Order of a Polynomial
problem: For the polynomial $f(x) = -3x^4 + x^2 + 4x,$ show that $f = \mathcal O(x)$ as $x\to 0.$
worked_solution:
We say $f(x)$ is of order $g(x)$ as $x\to a,$ and we write 

$$
f(x) = \mathcal O(g(x)) \quad \textrm{as}\quad x\to a
$$

if there exist ${\textrm{positive}}$ constants $K$ and $\delta$ such that

$$
{|f(x)| \leq K|g(x)|}
\quad\textrm{for all}\quad 0 < |x-a| < \delta.
$$

 

So, in our case, we need to show that

$$
{|f(x)| \leq K|x|}
 \quad \textrm{for} \quad {0 < |x| < \delta}.
$$

By the triangle inequality, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}|f(x)| & =|-3{x}^{4}+{x}^{2}+4x| \\  & \le |3{x}^{4}|+|{x}^{2}|+|4x| \\  & =3|x{|}^{4}+|x{|}^{2}+4|x|.\end{aligned}
$$

If $|x| < 1,$ then we have ${|x|^2 \lt |x|}.$ Also, since $|x|<1,$ we have $|x|^4 < |x|.$ Therefore,

$$
3|x|^4 \le 3|x|
\quad\text{and}\quad
|x|^2 \le |x|.
$$

Hence

$$
\begin{aligned}|f(x)| & \le 3|x{|}^{4}+|x{|}^{2}+4|x| \\  & \le 3|x|+|x|+4|x| \\  & =8|x|.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $|f(x)| \leq 8|x|$ whenever $|x| < 1.$ Thus, taking ${K=8}$ and ${\delta = 1}$ satisfies the definition, and we conclude that $f = \mathcal O(x)$ as $x\to 0.$
